blockMcqs.question: Which two ACID properties make recovery necessary?
blockMcqs.explanation: Atomicity requires all-or-nothing; Durability requires committed data survives crashes. Recovery enforces both.

blockMcqs.question: A power cut loses volatile memory but the disk is intact. This is a:
blockMcqs.explanation: System failure = OS crash or power loss. Volatile memory (buffer pool) is lost; the disk and its log survive.

blockMcqs.question: WAL requires that the log record is fsynced:
options: After the data page is written
At the same time as the data page
Before the data page is written
blockMcqs.explanation: Write-Ahead Logging means the log must be durable before the corresponding data page is written — ensuring the log always captures what happened.

blockMcqs.question: Which operation re-applies changes from committed transactions after a crash?
blockMcqs.explanation: REDO replays the after-images of committed transactions to restore durability. UNDO reverses uncommitted ones.

blockMcqs.question: Deferred update strategy only needs REDO, not UNDO. Why?
options: No dirty pages reach disk before commit
blockMcqs.explanation: Deferred update delays all writes until after commit. Nothing uncommitted ever reaches disk, so there is nothing to undo.

blockMcqs.question: What is the main benefit of checkpoints in recovery?
options: They eliminate the need for WAL
They limit how far back in the log recovery must go
They compress the log file automatically
blockMcqs.explanation: A checkpoint records that pages are flushed. Recovery starts from the last checkpoint, not the beginning of the log.

blockMcqs.question: What is the correct order of ARIES recovery phases?
blockMcqs.explanation: ARIES: Analysis identifies what was active at crash; Redo restores pre-crash disk state; Undo rolls back uncommitted transactions.

blockMcqs.question: ARIES uses steal + no-force. Which logging operations does this require?
blockMcqs.explanation: Steal means uncommitted dirty pages can reach disk (needs UNDO). No-force means committed pages may not reach disk at commit (needs REDO).
